passage: I'm Sabina, and three interviews had ended with the same polite line about my missing experience. Then Bhupen read my portfolio and said, "Start on the fifteenth." I have never forgotten that. So when I found that the pricing sheet Bhupen had sent to two clients used the old tax rate, my chest went tight. It felt ungrateful to point at a mistake made by the person who took a chance on me. I waited a day. Then I walked over with the sheet in hand and said, "I think this rate is outdated. Could we check?" Bhupen looked, groaned, and said, "Thank you. Send me the corrected version and I will call both clients." I understood then that being honest was one of the ways of saying thanks.

qa.q: What was wrong with the pricing sheet Bhupen sent to two clients?
qa.a: It used the old tax rate.

qa.q: Why did Sabina wait a day before speaking up?
qa.a: Sabina felt it would be ungrateful to point at a mistake made by the person who had taken a chance on Sabina.

qa.q: What made Sabina's way of raising the error work well?
qa.a: Sabina brought the sheet and asked whether the rate could be checked, so Bhupen could fix it quickly without feeling blamed.

qa.q: How did Bhupen react to the correction?
qa.a: Bhupen thanked Sabina and planned to call both clients, which shows candid input was welcome.

grounding: The narrator, grateful to a manager who gave a chance, still points out an error, showing thanks and honesty can go together.
